topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: I shouldn't have sold it. I mean, the mite brought a few silvers, and those coppers went straight to the miller for a sack of flour, but Old Bessie, she belonged to my son. He left the village years ago, taken by the city's false promises, but I remember how he clung to that bear, how it was his world. Now it's in some stranger’s hands, probably fodder for a yard sale. I told myself I was thinking of the family, making ends meet, but it's hard to shake the thought that I've lost a piece of the past. The soil is giving good this year, the Saints be praised, but nothing can grow where memories are pulled up by the roots.
